chapters.1: Zephaniah warns of a coming day of the Lord's judgment on Judah and Jerusalem for idolatry and complacency, describing it as a day of wrath, darkness, and distress affecting people of every social class. He warns that neither wealth nor status will be able to save anyone from it.
chapters.2: The prophet calls the humble to seek the Lord and righteousness so they might be sheltered when judgment comes, then pronounces specific judgment on surrounding nations: Philistia, Moab, Ammon, Ethiopia, and Assyria (including Nineveh), all of which will be devastated.
chapters.3: Zephaniah condemns Jerusalem's corrupt leaders, judges, prophets, and priests for their violence and unfaithfulness, but promises that God will purify a humble remnant who trust in him. The book ends on a joyful note, picturing God rejoicing over his people with singing and restoring their fortunes and reputation among the nations.
